name: nomina
description: Read-only financial markets research: ticker search, sourced price history, date-aligned comparisons, and a market overview. No API key, no account, no trading.
long_description:
Nomina gives Claude source-backed answers to market questions: which symbol is meant, what an asset has done over a period or an exact date window, how several assets compare on shared trading dates, and how the major indexes, rates, the dollar, gold, oil, BTC and ETH have moved.

Four read-only tools. search_markets finds Yahoo Finance symbols and dated headlines for a company, asset, sector, or topic. research_asset returns the latest quote, period return, drawdown and volatility, dated price history, and related headlines for one symbol. compare_assets aligns 2–6 symbols on shared session dates in their local currencies with an explicit adjusted-vs-raw price basis. market_overview reports period returns for a fixed basket of indexes, rates, commodities, and crypto. Every response carries source URLs, observation timestamps, and caveats, so Claude cites what the data shows and says what it does not.

Data comes from Yahoo Finance's public chart and search endpoints and can be delayed, unavailable, or rate-limited; this is research, not a real-time execution feed or a financial-statements service. Data rights are not included: Yahoo's terms restrict automated collection without permission and redistribution; review those terms before use. Only your search terms, symbols, and requested history period or date window are sent to Yahoo — Nomina stores no conversations or queries. Requires a Claude Desktop release with MCPB v0.4 UV-runtime support and internet access for the first install and for market queries.
